channel.title: ShopNow Kitchen
channel.description: Air fryers and meat thermometers, read from official listings. Conflicts printed, prices never quoted.

item.title: Basket or oven-style air fryer: what should you compare?
item.description: Form factor decides footprint, loading, and what fits. Start there, not with wattage.

item.title: A no-hype checklist for comparing air fryer capacity
item.description: Quarts describe a cavity, not a meal. Six checks before any number convinces you.

item.title: How to assess cleanup and counter-space trade-offs
item.description: Dishwasher-safe describes a part. It does not describe your evening.

item.title: Questions to ask before buying a multi-function kitchen appliance
item.description: Every extra preset is a control, a part and a failure point. Which three will you use?

item.title: Instant-read or wireless thermometer: which do you actually need?
item.description: Speed in your hand versus the freedom to walk away. Two different products.

item.title: How to assess thermometer accuracy claims
item.description: What ±0.5 °F, NIST and NSF mean on a listing — and what they do not.

item.title: Air fryer at Thanksgiving: what actually fits
item.description: A 12-inch pizza claim tells you more about usable size than a quart figure does.

item.title: Air fryer for a small kitchen: the three measurements that decide it
item.description: Depth, door swing and where it lives when it is not in use.

item.title: Your air fryer's first week: what to cook, what to skip
item.description: Three deliberate experiments, two things to skip, and the habit that earns the counter space.

item.title: Holiday hosting: how much air fryer capacity does a full table actually need?
item.description: Air fryer capacity is not quarts — it is layers and minutes. A holiday hosting worksheet with batch math.

item.title: The holiday roast question: when does a wireless thermometer actually earn its keep?
item.description: Doneness is a temperature, not a timer. USDA safe temperatures, probe placement, and the walk-away test for wireless probes.

item.title: Is your meat thermometer telling the truth? The two-minute ice-water test
item.description: USDA publishes the calibration check. Here it is step by step, and what a pass means when a listing claims plus or minus half a degree.

item.title: How to read an air fryer listing: what “Hi-Fry” and 24 presets actually tell you
item.description: The title, the bullets and the specification table are three different sources stapled onto one page. Here is which one to trust for which number.

item.title: Is a dual-basket air fryer worth it, or are you just buying two baskets?
item.description: Two zones pay off on exactly one condition. Check it against your own week before you spend anything on a second drawer.

item.title: Reheating leftovers is a temperature, not a microwave guess: the 165-degree rule
item.description: The USDA number for leftovers and casseroles, what a maximum-temperature line on an air fryer listing does and does not mean, and why this page has no minutes in it.

item.title: “cETL approved” and “NIST and NSF”: what a certification line on a spec sheet really promises
item.description: Two of the five listings on this site carry a safety-mark line and one carries a metrology acronym. Here is what each one can and cannot be asked to prove.

item.title: Gifting an appliance in December: the five checks that decide whether it gets used
item.description: Counter depth, doors, an app, a battery in the box and a warranty line. All five are answerable from the listing before you wrap anything.

item.title: First week with a leave-in probe: seven checks before a long cook depends on it
item.description: Pairing, the alert test across your own house, what a 1000-degree heat-safe figure refers to, and the two numbers one listing cannot agree on.
